name: max-pages
description:
Proves the max_pages parameter actually drives the paging bound rather than being decorative. The scenario passes max_pages=2 and serves three genuinely distinct full pages, so a walk bound by the parameter stops after two and a walk bound by the 20,000-page default would keep going.

Each page carries a full five hundred rows with ids that advance, so neither the short-page exit nor the no-progress check can fire: the ONLY thing that can end this walk is the ceiling, which is what makes the stop attributable to the parameter. The message is the safety-limit form, and it ends in the remediation clause -- the ceiling is a value the operator can raise, unlike a vendor-imposed one -- which log_contains pins verbatim.

when_exhausted is `empty` ONLY as a terminator for a regression: if the parameter stopped being read the walk would take the third page and then an empty one and end on its own one request later, failing on request_count and the missing log line rather than running to the default ceiling and timing out.

namespaced_ids is skipped for the reason recorded in happy and paged: the id is the bare NinjaOne device id with no tenant or instance scope.

log_contains: ninjaone: page limit of 2 hit (integration safety limit, retrieved 1000 assets, total not reported) - raise the max_pages parameter to import the rest
